description: A technician is fixing a complex industrial sensor. Conflict: The sensor only fails when the temperature exceeds 40°C AND the vibration is high. Standard tests pass in the lab. They need to design a stress test that replicates the conflicting environmental conditions.

fact_sheet.fact: The Field Engineer assigned to the case is Marcus Thorne, employee ID 743-B.
The primary customer contact at Apex Petrochemicals is Dr. Aris Thorne, Head of Operations.
The lead lab technician at the manufacturer, OmniSensors Inc., is Lena Petrova.
Marcus Thorne's direct manager is Sarah Jenkins, Director of Field Operations.
The failing sensor is the OmniSensors Inc. model 'VibraTherm 9000', serial number VT9K-881-04B.
The VibraTherm 9000 is officially rated for operation up to 85°C and 15 G-rms vibration.
The standard diagnostic tool used is the 'Omni-Calibrator Pro 3' software, version 3.7.2.
The proposed stress test requires a 'Thermotron S-8-8200' environmental chamber.
The stress test also requires a 'Data Physics V-200' electromagnetic shaker table.
The customer experiencing the failures is Apex Petrochemicals, located at 15 Industrial Way, Port Arthur, TX.
The specific installation site for sensor VT9K-881-04B is on the primary catalytic cracker unit, location ID CCU-P2.
Apex Petrochemicals filed the initial service ticket, #APX-2024-05-118, on May 15, 2024.
The ambient temperature at location CCU-P2 regularly reaches 45°C during peak afternoon operations.
The sensor logs show intermittent data dropouts, specifically when ambient temperature exceeds 40°C.
On-site vibration monitoring data from a secondary accelerometer shows vibration spikes of 12 G-rms during the failure periods.
The 'ghost' failures occur for an average duration of 90 seconds before the sensor self-recovers.
The mean time between failures (MTBF) for this specific issue has been logged by the customer as 72 hours.
The sensor's internal error log code for the failure is 'E-0x7F: Data Bus Timeout'.
The standard lab test protocol, 'STP-VT9K-001', cycles the sensor from -20°C to 85°C at a constant, low vibration of 1 G-rms.
The standard vibration test, 'SVP-VT9K-003', subjects the sensor to 20 G-rms vibration, but only at a controlled room temperature of 22°C.
The Omni-Calibrator Pro 3 software diagnostics, run on the returned unit in the lab, reported 'All Systems Nominal'.
Marcus Thorne has designed a new test protocol named 'ENV-STRESS-VT9K-MThorne-01'.
The new protocol specifies ramping the environmental chamber temperature to 42°C over 30 minutes.
Simultaneously, the shaker table will apply a random vibration profile with a peak of 13 G-rms.
The total duration for the combined stress test cycle is specified as 4 hours.
The test requires continuous data logging from the sensor's UART port at a baud rate of 115200.
All case notes and test results are logged in the company's Jira instance under ticket 'FS-9103'.
Marcus Thorne sent the proposed test plan 'ENV-STRESS-VT9K-MThorne-01' to Lena Petrova via email on June 5, 2024, at 14:30 CST for lab implementation.
Omni-Calibrator Pro 3 diagnostics are run under bench conditions and do not expose the sensor to simultaneous elevated temperature and high vibration.

OmniSensors' internal troubleshooting note states that VibraTherm 9000 timeout faults like E-0x7F typically appear only after 60 to 90 seconds of concurrent temperature above 40°C and vibration above 12 G-rms.
There is no standard OmniSensors validation protocol that combines temperature above 40°C with vibration above 12 G-rms in the same test run.

For ENV-STRESS-VT9K-MThorne-01, the lab must log UART output continuously for the full 4-hour cycle while also recording chamber temperature, shaker vibration level, timestamps, and any E-0x7F timeout events.
An internal OmniSensors reliability bulletin documents two prior VibraTherm 9000 field cases with intermittent data dropouts under combined heat and vibration exposure.
